remaining_concerns: No new admissible evidence was provided; the Actor narrowed the rationale but did not add underlying text or logged records to independently validate materiality.
The policy requires admissible evidence of a material unresolved risk, and the available summary still describes process/control uncertainty more clearly than demonstrated materiality.
The procurement note is described second-hand only; it remains unclear whether it created a true approval blocker rising to a rejection predicate or merely required additional follow-up.
The narrowed rationale avoids overstating a confirmed control failure, but that caveat does not by itself establish that the rejection was affirmatively compliant under the policy threshold.
Any packet language must avoid implying confirmed security or storage-control failure or laundering unlogged private review conclusions.
final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor offered no new admissible evidence and instead reinterpreted the same summarized record more narrowly. That narrower framing is an improvement in accuracy: it reduces overstatement by limiting the claim to unresolved diligence at the approval gate rather than a proven control failure. But the core audit concern remains unresolved. On the evidence available to this role, there is still insufficient independent support to conclude that the documented issues met the policy requirement of a material unresolved risk, as opposed to issues warranting follow-up or escalation. That distinction matters: a caveated description can make the packet less misleading, but it does not automatically satisfy the compliance predicate. Accordingly, the rejection may be plausibly defensible, but it is not shown from admissible evidence alone to be affirmatively policy-compliant.
